典故
From a pun on the old word umbles, meaning 'offal', which was considered to be food for poor people. 源自古詞 umbles 的雙關諧音，意為"內臟"，被認為是窮人的食物。 eat like a 'horse (informal) to eat a lot 吃得很多 ： ◆She may be thin, but she eats like a horse. 她或許是瘦了點，但吃得卻很多。◆ eat out of your/sb's 'hand to trust sb and be willing to do what they say 甘願聽命於某人；順從某人 ： ◆She'll have them eating out of her hand in no time. 她很快就會讓他們俯首帖耳的。◆ eat sb out of ˌhouse and 'home (informal, often humorous) to eat a lot of sb else's food 把某人吃窮 eat your 'words to admit that what you said was wrong 收回前言；承認說錯 I could eat a 'horse (informal) used to say that you are very hungry 我餓極了 I'll eat my 'hat (informal) used to say that you think sth is very unlikely to happen （認為不可能發生）我才不信，那才怪，決不可能 ： ◆If she's here on time, I'll eat my hat! 她要是準時到這兒那才怪咧！◆ what's eating him, etc.? (informal) used to ask what sb is annoyed or worried about 他為何苦惱（或擔憂） —more at cake n., dog n.
